title: Prefetch stabilizer for crossplane KV tiling with continuous batching
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Large multi-GPU inference workloads show oscillating prefetch activity when continuous batching interacts with pipeline/tensor parallel boundaries. The oscillation causes repeated KV slice migrations between GPUs, transient memory pressure spikes, and throughput variance for tail-latency-sensitive requests. This ticket implements a prefetch stabilizer: a lightweight coordinator + local heuristics that dampen prefetch oscillation, smooth KV slice handoffs across pipeline boundaries, and reduce unnecessary cross-GPU memory churn while preserving latency SLOs for streaming requests.
technical_design:
Overview:
- Coordinator model: per-node 'stabilizer agent' that aggregates lightweight signals (batch size histogram, active stream prefixes, KV hotness score, GPU memory headroom) and exposes a small state-machine for handoff decisions.
- Local heuristics: each GPU keeps a ring-buffer of recent access footprints (slice IDs, sequence length buckets, hit/miss) to compute a moving hotness score and preferred placement affinity.
- Handoff protocol: instead of immediate reactive migration on first hotness crossing, we implement a staged handoff: advertise -> grace-window -> prefetch-buffered-move -> commit. The grace-window length is adaptive to observed batch inter-arrival time distribution.
- Continuous batching interaction: stabilizer observes stream batching cadence and clamps prefetch rate when cadence is bursty. Batching-aware prefetch throttling uses a token-bucket keyed by stream and adjusted by measured latency impact.
- Pipeline/tensor parallel coordination: handoffs across pipeline boundaries piggyback on existing RPC channels (no new synchronous round-trips). Agents exchange compact summaries (slice range + estimated KV delta + token count).
- Memory safety: prefetches are allocated to a reserved spill-window region; if memory pressure grows, the policy prefers returning slices to the origin GPU rather than immediate eviction.
- Backpressure and fallback: if the stabilizer detects rising miss-rate with violated latency SLO, it disables staged handoffs and falls back to immediate local prefetch (fast but higher churn) until stable state resumes.
Data structures and formats:
- Compact slice descriptor: 16 bytes (start_index, length, hotness_epoch, checksum) for RPCs.
- Ring buffer: bounded size 256 entries per GPU, stores (slice_id, seq_bucket, hit_bool, timestamp).
Parameters exposed to config:
- grace_window_ms (default 15ms), prefetch_rate_limit_ops (default 500 ops/s), ring_size (default 256), hotness_threshold (0.75), spill_window_bytes (default 128MB).
Implementation notes:
- Minimal changes to runtime: stabilizer is an opt-in module behind a runtime flag --kv-stabilizer.
- Instrumentation: add per-stream histograms, prefetch counters, handoff commit/abort counters to Console metrics.
- Tests: microbenchmarks for handoff latency, integration test with continuous-batching simulator, stress test for memory churn on heterogeneous GPU sets.
acceptance_criteria:
- Stabilizer agent can be enabled/disabled via runtime flag and config.
- In synthetic continuous-batching simulator, enable stabilizer reduces cross-GPU KV migrations by >= 35% compared to baseline while keeping p99 token latency within 10% of baseline for streaming requests.
- Metrics emitted: stabilizer.handoffs.advertised, stabilizer.handoffs.committed, stabilizer.handoffs.aborted, stabilizer.prefetch.throttled_ops, stabilizer.memory.spill_window_usage.
- Integration test passes on heterogeneous multi-GPU topology (2x A100 + 2x A30 equivalent) with pipeline parallel depth 2.
- Code review and one successful canary rollout to internal staging with observability dashboards linked.
rollout_plan:
1) Merge feature branch behind feature flag. 2) Canary on internal staging with small traffic (5% of internal test traffic) for 48 hours. 3) Monitor stabilizer metrics and p99 latency; if regressions > 10% abort. 4) Gradual ramp to 25% then 100% over 1 week. 5) Post-rollout retrospective and tuning of defaults.
Emergency rollback: flip --kv-stabilizer=false and disable cross-GPU prefetching in orchestration policy.
progress_updates: 2026-03-02: Spike completed: simulated continuous-batching workload and reproduced oscillatory prefetch with current runtime. Measured baseline migration churn metric ~420 migrations/min.
2026-03-05: Prototype of ring-buffer hotness estimator implemented; initial experiments show hotness smoothing reduces false-positive migrations by ~28%.
2026-03-08: Implemented staged handoff state-machine and lightweight RPC summaries. Integration tests added to CI. Initial canary plan drafted.
2026-03-12: Tuned grace_window_ms from 50ms->15ms after observing increased tail latency in low-concurrency tests; updated acceptance criteria accordingly. Preparing PR for code review.
review_feedback: 2026-03-09 - PM (Sofia Ramos): Ensure we expose a customer-visible knob to prefer throughput vs stability; recommend a 'conservative' preset for enterprise tenants.
2026-03-10 - Infra (Jamal Ortiz): Confirmed RPC summary stays <64 bytes to avoid extra PCIe traffic; requested microbench of RPC CPU overhead.
2026-03-11 - Security (Lena Kaur): No customer data in slice descriptors; approve but ask to document zeroing behavior for spilled buffers.
notes:
Trade-offs considered:
- Aggressive prefetching reduces request latency but increases churn; we choose staged handoff to bias toward stability for long-lived streams.
- We intentionally avoid centralized global placement decisions to reduce coordination overhead and single point of failure; per-node agents make probabilistic decisions based on compact signals.
- This design focuses on continuous-batching and streaming traffic; latency-critical single-shot queries should bypass staged handoff via route-level policy.
Open questions:
- Default grace_window sizing under mixed workloads needs more field data.
- Evaluate interactions with quantization-induced memory savings (may reduce need for spill-window).
